name: Ira
overview: Ira was a male warrior known as the Ithrite and was the thirty-fifth member of "the thirty," an elite group of David's men. Beyond his designation as the Ithrite and his position among David's warriors, Scripture does not provide additional details about his tribal affiliation or personal background.
namesAndTitles: The name Ira is a proper name that may mean "stallion donkey," according to its Hebrew origin. There is no indication that this name was given directly by God, and it appears simply as a personal identifier in the biblical record.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Ira beyond what is listed in his unique attribute as a member of David's thirty. No additional familial connections are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Ira's significance lies in his role as one of David's elite warriors, specifically as the thirty-fifth of "the thirty," highlighting his valor and trusted position within David's military leadership. His designation as the Ithrite associates him with a particular lineage or clan, though details are sparse. This inclusion in the list of David's mighty men underscores the importance of faithful and courageous followers in the establishment of David's kingdom.
